jurisdiction.name: Guyana
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Guyana has no AI-specific law, strategy or guideline; AI is promoted through presidential and ministerial digitalisation announcements. The only binding AI-relevant rule is the right not to be subject to automated decision-making in the Data Protection Act 2023, which is still awaiting a commencement order.
lead_institutions: Office of the Prime Minister / Ministry of Public Service (digital transformation)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from Parliament's acts and bills listings and government websites. The Official Gazette could only be searched through web search. The ICT Master Plan 2030 and the government's announced AI initiatives have no published policy text and are tracked as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Guyana (National Assembly), assented by the President
instruments.current_status: Passed by the National Assembly on 9 August 2023 (Bill No. 14 of 2023), assented on 16 August 2023 and published in the Official Gazette Legal Supplement A of the same date. Section 1 brings it into operation on a day (or days, per provision) appointed by ministerial order; no commencement order was found on the Parliament or Official Gazette sites on 2026-10-12, so no commencement date is given (see Leads).
instruments.summary: Guyana's general data protection law regulating the collection, keeping, processing, use and dissemination of personal data by public authorities and private controllers, built on GDPR-style principles, lawful bases, data subject rights, cross-border transfer rules and a Data Protection Commissioner. Section 19 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for contract, authorising law or consent and a duty on controllers to implement safeguards. Access rights include information on the existence of automated decision-making and meaningful information about the logic involved.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding Guyanese law found with explicit rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Guyana were searched, including Parliament's lists of acts and bills, the official gazette, ministries and regulators. The Data Protection Act 2023, which covers automated decision-making, was recorded; no national AI strategy, AI bill or other AI-specific material was found. Not yet verified from the official text: whether the Data Protection Act 2023 has come into force, the ICT Master Plan 2030, and the gazette, telecommunications agency and consumer commission sites, which were searched only indirectly.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. officialgazette.gov.gy: no usable full-text search (web search only); Telecommunications Agency and CCAC sites not opened. DPA 2023 source: Parliament Acts page (PDF link session-bound, official_pdf_url null); scanned Gazette Legal Supplement A (16 Aug 2023) read as images (cover, s.1, s.19, final page); rest cross-checked against Bill on mola.gov.gy. No commencement order found. Open Data Act 2024, ETA 2023, Digital ID Act 2023, Cybercrime Act: not AI-specific. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Parliament Acts of Parliament list (2023-2025) and Bill Status list browsed; Official Gazette searched by web search. Found Data Protection Act 2023 (s.19 automated decision-making). Open Data Act 2024, Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 2023, Digital Identity Card Act 2023 and Cybercrime Act not AI-specific. No AI bill, deepfake offence or public-sector algorithm rule found.; Government: Searched, nothing found: no national AI strategy, AI policy or public-sector/GenAI guideline document; AI agenda exists only in speeches and DPI news (leads). ICT Master Plan 2030 text not found.; Ministries: Education, Health, Public Service, Home Affairs/police, Legal Affairs searched: announcements only, no AI policy documents.; Regulators: Data Protection Commissioner/Office not yet operational, no AI guidance; Bank of Guyana, NDMA/CIRT (cyber), telecom regulator: searched, nothing AI-specific found.. Not reached: Official Gazette site search (officialgazette.gov.gy has no full-text search usable without bulk download; covered via web search only); Telecommunications Agency and Competition and Consumer Affairs Commission sites not opened individually. Could not verify: Commencement status of the Data Protection Act 2023; Existence/content of the ICT Master Plan 2030. strategy, government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
